clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient’s most pressing issue is isolated diastolic hypertension, which drives cardiovascular risk and aligns with documented BP readings. A constellation of metabolic risk factors (obesity, prediabetes, dyslipidemia) fulfills metabolic syndrome criteria, further compounding risk. Early renal dysfunction is suggested by rising BUN/creatinine, while prediabetes, fatty liver risk, and psychosocial stressors add layers of complexity. Secondary causes of hypertension (renal artery stenosis, thyroid disease) and other comorbidities remain possible but lack supporting data, necessitating targeted work‑up.
